description: Goal-intention ranking treats planning as *goal recognition*: it asks how well the facts a search path made true match the goal. It samples many relaxed plans to the goal and gives each fact a probability `P(q | G)` from how often its achievers appear in them; a second set of samples gives `P(q | ¬G)` for plans that do not aim at the goal. `ol_rp` ranks a path by the negative log likelihood of its observed facts, and `op_rp` by the negative log ratio of the two probabilities; lower means more goal-directed. These are ranking keys, not distances: they are not admissible and never prove a dead end. Use them as a tie-breaker in search, for example in BFWS, with `IntentionTracker` to carry them along each path.

papers.authors: Giacomo Rosa, Jean Honorio, Nir Lipovetzky, Sebastian Sardina
papers.title: Planning as Goal Recognition: Deriving Heuristics from Intention Models -- Extended Version
